The attempt to link the Atlantic Ocean (reached by the Pee Dee River‑Winyah Bay system) with the Pacific through the continental isthmus of Central America was led by the French diplomat **Ferdinand de Lesseps**.  

After his triumph with the Suez Canal, Lesseps championed a sea‑level canal proposal in the 1880s that would run through the Panama isthmus – the region that includes the El Valle volcano. This French venture ultimately failed, but it laid the groundwork for the later United States undertaking that led to the modern Panama Canal.
